title: Investigation of the effects of a 6% hypertonic sodium chloride solution on the reduction of mucus plugs in COPD patients – A prospective, non-interventional pilot study
summary: The primary objectives of this open-label, non-interventional, single-arm, single-center pilot study are: to investigate the efficacy of 6% hypertonic saline (HS)* in reducing mucus plugs in patients with COPD (GOLD stages II–IV); to evaluate the impact on the quality of life of COPD patients; and to analyze potential correlations between the mucus plug (MP) score, sputum quality, and inflammatory markers.

interventions.name: MucoClear 6% (6% sodium chloride inhalation solution), a CE-certified inhalation solution routinely used in the treatment of COPD patients.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Confirmed COPD diagnosis (GOLD stage II–IV)
• Mucus plug score of ≥1 on CT imaging
• Dyspnea of ​​primarily pulmonary origin
• Written informed consent for study participation
• Patients prescribed hypertonic sodium chloride solution (6%) as part of their routine care
• Ability and willingness to perform the prescribed inhalation therapy
• Patients with exacerbations requiring antibiotics in the 3–6 months prior to study start may be included
• Stable disease phase (no acute exacerbation within the 8 weeks prior to study start)
• Ability to understand and comply with study requirements
• Willingness to attend scheduled follow-up visits over the 12-week study period
Exclusion criteria:
• Acute exacerbation within the 8 weeks prior to study start
• Cystic fibrosis
• Clinical history of asthma
• Severe cardiac, hepatic, or renal insufficiency
• Pregnancy or breastfeeding
• Intolerance to hypertonic sodium chloride solutions
• Active smokers
• Patients undergoing endobronchial lung volume reduction (ELVR)
• Recent changes in airway medication or health status within 4 weeks prior to study start
• Active lung cancer
• Patients experiencing exacerbations requiring antibiotics during the study will be excluded from the analysis
• Administration of additional mucolytic agents
